prompt.context: Your client, Congo.com (named after one of Earth's rainforests), is one of the largest e-commerce retailers in the world. It specializes in a diverse logistics network, and its brand is built around consumer satisfaction. The company has grown dramatically over the last 5 years, but has started to notice recent profit margin dips.
prompt.question: You have been hired to find the root causes that Congo must address to focus on profitability so they can continue to drive growth. Any positive change in profitability is the goal — it is up to you to quantify the impact of changes recommended.

clarifying_info.q: What does Congo prioritize for customers?
clarifying_info.a: Congo gives its customers the best prices with the fastest delivery rates.

clarifying_info.q: Which geography are we focused on?
clarifying_info.a: Congo is a worldwide company, but wants to focus on US profitability to drive expansion into other countries.

clarifying_info.q: How many distribution facilities does Congo operate in the US?
clarifying_info.a: There are eight main distribution facilities in the United States.

clarifying_info.q: How has Congo grown relative to competitors?
clarifying_info.a: Company growth has outpaced all competitors in the retail industry.
Profit margin = net income / total revenue.

exhibits.title: Congo.com Income Statement (US Distribution Centers only, unaudited, in millions)
exhibits.shows: A table with years 2013–2017 showing Units Shipped, Avg $/unit, Total Revenue, and line-item Operating Expenses (Maintenance, SG&A, Transportation, Permitting, Other), then NI Pre Tax, Taxes, and Net Income.

exhibits.title: Congo.com US Distribution Network – 2017
exhibits.shows: A bar chart for each of 7 US distribution centers (ABE8, AVP1, CLT2, CVG3, FTW1, MDW2, ONT8) comparing Units per day, Operating Costs ($/day), and Transportation Costs ($/day), with facility square footage noted.

exhibits.title: Trailer Utilization for >5-Year-Old Facilities (2013–2017)
exhibits.shows: A dual-axis chart showing Daily Trailers Shipped (bar) and Trailer Utilization % (line) from 2013 to 2017, plus a project proposal box. A table lists each facility's age in years.

project_proposal.description: Automation upgrades allow under-performing facilities to improve trailer utilization to company standards; current automation standards implemented in all facilities built within last 5 years.

framework: Profitability = Revenue – Costs; diagnose which side is driving margin decline
Revenue analysis: Units shipped (volume) vs. Avg $/unit (price), trend over 2013–2017
Cost analysis: Break down each cost line as % of revenue; identify which cost is growing disproportionately
Identify Transportation costs as the primary driver (40%→60% of revenue 2015→2017)
Drill into distribution network to pinpoint which facilities have elevated transportation cost%
Determine root cause within transportation: lane costs, trailer utilization, or DOT costs
Quantify savings opportunity from addressing root cause; calculate impact on Net Income
Recommend investments with cost/benefit analysis and next steps

questions.prompt: Review Exhibit 1. What is driving the recent decline in profit margins at Congo.com?
questions.guidance: Candidate should note Net Income rose from $20M (2014) to $651M (2016) then fell to $300M (2017). Revenue grew 19% YoY in 2017 yet NI nearly halved. The key insight is that Transportation costs jumped from 40% to 50% to 60% of revenue (2015→2016→2017) while Maintenance and SG&A have been stable or declining as % of revenue. Avg $/unit is market-driven and Congo has little control. The candidate should conclude Transportation costs are the root cause.

math.setup: NI margin 2016 vs 2017: 5.60% vs 2.16%. Transportation as % of revenue: 2015=40%, 2016=50%, 2017=60%.
steps: Increase in Transportation % of revenue from 2015 to 2017: +20 percentage points
All other cost lines were stable or declining as % of revenue
math.answer: Transportation cost inflation (from 40% to 60% of revenue) is the primary driver of margin compression.

questions.prompt: Review Exhibit 2. Which distribution centers represent the best opportunity to reduce transportation costs, and why?
questions.guidance: Candidate should note: FTW1 ships the most units/day among 500k sq ft facilities (4 units/sq ft — highest productivity in network) yet has 80% transportation cost %. AVP1 also has 80% transportation cost %. The other 5 facilities are at 60% transportation cost %. FTW1 and AVP1 are the two outliers. Bonus: candidate recognizes AVP1 even though it ships fewer units/day.

math.setup: Unit/Sq.Ft. ratio by facility from interviewer guidance sheet.
steps: FTW1: 500k sq ft, 4 units/sq ft — highest productivity, but 80% transport cost %
AVP1: 500k sq ft, 3 units/sq ft, 80% transport cost %
CLT2, ABE8, CVG3, MDW2, ONT8: all at 60% transport cost %
math.answer: FTW1 and AVP1 are best improvement opportunities (80% vs 60% transport cost %); FTW1 has highest productivity (4 units/sq ft).

questions.prompt: Transportation costs have three components: lane costs, trailer utilization, and US DOT costs. Given Congo is expanding shipping destinations, which factor should we investigate?
questions.guidance: As Congo expands destinations, lane costs and DOT costs should naturally rise — they are tied to volume/geography and harder to control. Trailer utilization is the lever Congo can directly manage. Candidate should zero in on utilization for FTW1 and/or AVP1. Interviewer should give Exhibit 3 once candidate identifies trailer utilization as the key investigation area.

questions.prompt: Review Exhibit 3 and the Project Proposal. Calculate the annual transportation cost savings if Congo invests in automation upgrades at eligible facilities. What is the impact on Net Income?
questions.guidance: Eligible facilities are those older than 5 years: AVP1 (7 years) and FTW1 (8 years). Automation would cut transportation costs by 25% at each. Candidate must read daily transportation costs from Exhibit 2 bar chart. Using the interviewer guidance data: FTW1 transport cost = $1.6M/day, AVP1 = $1.2M/day. Assume 350 operating days/year. Strong candidates will identify both facilities; if only one is identified, calculate for that one only.

math.setup: From Exhibit 2 interviewer data: FTW1 transport cost = $1.6M/day; AVP1 transport cost = $1.2M/day. Saving = 25% of daily cost × 350 days.
steps: New NI Pre-Tax (both): $429M + $245M = $674M (~60% increase in NI)
math.answer: Total annual transportation savings of $245M, increasing Net Income ~60% (from $300M to ~$504M after tax, or $674M pre-tax). Payback period under 1 month.

questions.prompt: (Bonus / time permitting) If trailer utilization at eligible facilities improves from 40% to 60%, what is the new number of daily trailers shipped in 2017?
questions.guidance: This is an algebraic relationship: total SKU volume shipped is constant; utilization determines how many trailers are needed to carry that volume.

math.setup: 2017 daily trailers = 1407 (round to 1400); 2017 utilization = 40% (meaning 60% of each trailer is empty). Find volume constant, then recalculate trailers at 60% utilization.
math.answer: 1,225 daily trailers shipped (down from 1,407), a reduction of ~13%.

recommendation: Congo should invest $20M in automation upgrades at AVP1 and FTW1 (the two facilities older than 5 years), which will reduce their transportation costs by 25%.
This yields approximately $245M in annual transportation savings, increasing Net Income by ~60% (from ~$300M to ~$504M after tax) with a payback period under one month.

Congo should also study the operational and productivity practices at high-efficiency facilities (especially FTW1's 4 units/sq ft benchmark) and implement them at other facilities to raise network-wide output.
Further automation investment across the network could also reduce SG&A costs over time.
risks: Implementation disruption: automation upgrades at active facilities may temporarily reduce throughput
Execution cost overruns beyond the $10M/facility estimate
Dependency on US Department of Transportation regulations and costs, which are partly outside Congo's control
Higher automation typically leads to higher maintenance costs over time
next_steps: Engage firm to help renegotiate trailer contracts to lock in savings alongside utilization improvements
Prepare the broader distribution network for higher utilization and higher productivity standards
Evaluate automation roadmap for remaining 5 facilities to capture additional SG&A and operational efficiencies
Monitor Avg $/unit pricing competitiveness as Congo scales volume
